reason: Re-opened packet.js quran 58 --verse 51.56: al-Tabari's one comment on 51:56 to 51:57 gives Zayd b. Aslam's reading and Ibn Abbas's (to acknowledge servitude willingly or unwillingly), then says in his own voice that Ibn Abbas's is the more correct (awla al-qawlayn bi-al-sawab), glossed as created for Our worship and humbling to Our amr, and answers the objection: the deniers have humbled themselves to His qada', which runs over them and they cannot refuse, and the disbeliever opposes Him only in acting on what He commanded. Evidence words found verbatim. The revision carries this without drift: 'with Ibn Abbas' reports his stated preference (trap satisfied); 'bow to Him' generalises tadhallul li-amrina, which his own answer then specifies as the decree; 'yield to His decree' is tadhallalu li-qada'ihi; 'resisting only His bidding' is khalafahu fi al-'amal bima amarahu bihi. The earlier command/command paradox is gone. Plain sense checked in day.js: 51:54 to 51:55 tell the Prophet to withdraw and to warn, and 51:56 turns to the singular first person; no four-word run from the key verse. No school needed, no comparison, tone plain. verse.js ok (Adh-Dhariyat 51:56, at 4730); entry-check ok, no warns. Residual weakness, not a break: 'takes them' has no antecedent inside the sentence and leans on the key verse printed above.
